## New Skills and Talents
The Skills and Talents below are new options for Dwarf Characters to spend XP on. These Skills and Talents cannot be used by non-Dwarf Characters unless the GM rules otherwise. 

## **New Skills**
This section includes two new Specialisations for existing Skills, and a brand new Skill. 

## **Lore (Runes)**
## **(Int), Advanced, Specialisation**
Runelore covers a Dwarf ’s knowledge of the history, processes, and effects of magical runes (page 121). Characters can use the Skill to anticipate what materials are useful for crafting a rune, and where those materials can be found. It covers knowledge of famous Runesmiths — what their masterworks were, and the sagas of their original creation. Besides identifying runes and their powers, the Specialisation also covers knowledge of Dwarf magical secrets, such as how to reveal faded or invisible inscriptions. 

By convention, a Runesmith’s Apprentice must demonstrate encyclopaedic knowledge of their craft before they are allowed to actually forge their first rune. Unlike most Lore Specialisations, runelore cannot be learned from books. The Runesmiths Guild are forever paranoid that their secrets will fall into unworthy hands, so pass on their lore directly via oral tradition. 

## **Runesmithing**
## **Sail (Skycraft)**
## **(Ag), Advanced, Specialisation**
The Skycraft Specialisation is used to fly gyrocopters, airships, war balloons and other flying machines. Like the normal Sail Skill, it is not just used for piloting the vehicle, but for other activities related to the routine operation of the vehicle, like tying knots, or refuelling under fire. Tests of Sail (Skycraft) are only necessary when pushing a machine beyond its usual capabilities, but the experimental nature of skycraft could mean that Tests are necessary more often than for tried-and-true naval designs. Take-off and landing always require an **Average (+20)** Test, with failed Tests delaying departure, or inflicting damage on the vehicle, its occupants, or the landing zone. 

Unlike other Sail Specialisations, the procedures for operating a skycraft are sufficiently exotic that you cannot operate a skycraft unless you have Advances in the Sail (Skycraft) Specialisation. Furthermore, if a Character’s only Sail Specialisation is in Skycraft, they do not treat other Sail Specialisations as a Basic Skill. 

## **New Talents**
The following Talents are unique to Dwarf Characters. 

## **Ancestral Grudge**
**Max** : Willpower Bonus 

There are entries in the Great Book of Grudges — those borne against Orcs, Goblins, and Skaven in particular — that are so grievous they can only be avenged with the extinction of all their kind. You have inherited one of these fabled grudges, and whilst you have no chance of seeing it completed in your lifetime, you are more than happy to do your part. 

## **(Dex), Advanced**
Runesmithing is used for crafting magical runes, and to harness magic to reawaken or deactivate runes forged by others. It is a difficult, exacting Skill, that requires formidable concentration, with none of the immediate flashy effects of conventional spellcraft. 

Whilst training and understanding is a critical part of Runesmithing, much of the process is conducted by gut instinct, and subconscious attunement with magical forces. This distinguishes the Skill from Lore (Runes) — any Dwarf can learn runelore if given the chance, but only a few have the gift to transmute the Winds of Magic into physical form. See the Runic Magic chapter on page 121 for more about using the Runesmithing Skill. 

Choose a culture or faction that is the target of your Ancestral Grudge (e.g. Orcs, Goblins, Skaven, Trolls, Daemons of Khorne, etc.). Enter them into your Book of Grudges as the target of your vengeance, per the rules on page 33. 

You bear this group a Blood Grudge that can never be satisfied. However, every time you win a significant victory against this group — e.g. by destroying their works, taking back something stolen, or killing many of their kind — you gain 50 XP. 

Each time you purchase this Talent, you gain an Ancestral Grudge against a different faction. At the GM’s discretion, declaring vengeance against a smaller sub-faction can award more XP when you score victory over them — e.g. you gain 75 XP each victory if your target is a specific Goblin tribe, or 100 XP each victory if targeting a specific Human family line. 

## **Bludgeoner**
**Max** : Strength Bonus 

**Tests** : Strength Tests when activating _Pummel_ Quality You smash more powerful enemies into submission with brutal hammer swings to the head, leaving them utterly exposed whilst you finish them off. When you win an opposed Test to activate the _Pummel_ Quality, you inflict an additional _Stunned_ Condition for each level of Bludgeoner. 

## **Crew Commander**
**Max** : Initiative bonus 

**Tests** _Crewed_ : Ranged Tests when firing weapon with the Flaw 

You are practised at managing crews of siege weapons and artillery pieces. As an Action you may make a **Challenging (+0) Leadership** Test to help a crew manning a weapon with the _Crewed_ Flaw within earshot. If you succeed, the crew members may use your Ranged Skill on the next attack using the weapon. 

_Blackpowder_ Quality, When you fire a weapon with the targeted enemies who fail their Cool Test gain an additional _Broken_ Condition for each level of Dragon Belcher. 

## **Entrenchment**
## **Max** : Intelligence Bonus
**Tests** : Trade when constructing protective cover You make the most of whatever terrain is available to you to protect yourself and allies from enemy missile fire. When you are in soft cover, attacks against you are **Hard (-20)** instead of **Difficult (-10)** . When you are in medium cover, attacks against you are **Very Hard (-30)** instead of **Hard (-20)** . 

## **Forgefire**
## **Max** : 1
You are a living battery of runic power, radiating an aura of battle-fury that imbues nearby weapons with the heat of their forging. When you are Engaged, any melee weapons wielded by yourself or an ally within Willpower Bonus yards gain the _Penetrating_ Quality. If an affected weapon is already _Penetrating_ , its attacks now ignore 1 additional point of non-metal armour. 

## **Glorious Demise**
## **Max** : 1
Your bloodlust is so strong it overwhelms your body’s natural instinct to rest after trauma. 

## **Demolisher**
**Max** : Strength Bonus 

**Tests** : Melee when breaking inanimate objects using a _Hack_ weapon 

Cover and armour is no defence against the bite of your axe. When you activate the _Hack_ Quality as part of an attack, you inflict +1 additional Damage on struck armour or shields for each level of Demolisher. In addition, when attacking an enemy in cover with a weapon that has the _Hack_ Quality, hard cover counts as medium cover, medium cover counts as soft cover, and soft cover provides no protection at all. 

## **Dragon Belcher**
## **Max** : Ballistic Skill Bonus
Certain Goblin tribes have been known to refer to Dwarf firearms as ‘dragon belchers’, for the furious roar and explosion of smoke they discharge as they fire. You make the most of this psychological impact to scatter and pin your opponents with suppressive fire. 

When you gain the _Unconscious_ Condition, you can interrupt the Turn order to make an immediate Melee attack as a Free Action, before you are taken out of action. 

When you gain the _Stunned_ Condition, you can spend a Fortune point to make an immediate Melee attack as a Free Action. You take your next Turn as usual, which means you cannot take an Action if you’re still _Stunned_ . 

## **Harpooner**
## **Max** : Ballistic Skill Bonus
As a veteran quareller, you use precision shooting to neutralise your target, impaling them with bolts in extremely painful locations. 

When you inflict a Critical Hit with a Crossbow weapon, you may increase your roll on the Critical Hit table by +10 for each level of Harpooner, to a maximum of 00. In addition, Crossbow bolts lodged into the target’s body due to the _Impale_ Quality reduce the target’s Movement by 1 per bolt, to a minimum of 1. 

**Kingsguard Max** : 3 

You are sworn to defend the life of your lord, and any they designate under your protection. If that means sacrificing your own life to shield your charge, you are prepared to do so. 

Any enemy attacks against an ally within 2 yards of you suffers a -10 modifier for each level of Kingsguard. This Talent does not apply to attacks against yourself, nor does it apply if you are currently suffering from a Condition. 

## **Liquid Fortification**
## **Max** : Toughness Bonus
**Tests** : Consume Alcohol 

Many Dwarfs insist that good ale can steady the nerves and improve the fighting proficiency of a hearty warrior. Nonetheless, a prudent fighter is careful not to become too reliant on alcohol, lest they become afflicted with “brew-fever”. 

You gain +10 Strength and Toughness after consuming an alcoholic drink. This provides an immediate bonus to your Consume Alcohol Test for consuming the drink, and the benefit continues to apply whether you succeed or fail on that Test. You retain this bonus until an hour has passed since your last alcoholic drink — drinking again can prolong the effect, but does not increase your Characteristic bonuses beyond +10. 

## **Long Memory**
**Max** : Intelligence Bonus 

**Tests** : Intelligence Tests to remember 

You never forget a face — or a promise. Unlike the Elven _Tower of Memories_ technique ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ), which Dwarfs consider frivolous and flawed, you use a form of sense memory to anchor details in the real places where you witnessed them, by recalling a specific feeling, taste, or smell from that location. 

When recalling significant events you were involved in previously in the campaign, you can perfectly remember the time, date, location, and visible faces of all individuals present, and exactly what those present pledged to say or do. If recalling a significant event you witnessed before the campaign began, you may need to take an Intelligence Test to remember details, with a difficulty set by the intervening time — Easy (+40) for events mere months ago, Hard (-20) for events a century ago. 

## **Magic Defiance**
## **Max** : Willpower Bonus
**Tests** : Willpower Tests to use _Magic Resistance_ ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ) 

You ground enemy spellcraft through your own body, refusing to be affected by its fickle enchantments. You can Reverse any Test you are obliged to make as part of a magic spell’s effects, as well as Tests to dispel magic with _Magic Resistance_ ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ). 

## **Master Rune Magic**
**Max** : Willpower Bonus 

**Tests** : Runesmithing 

You have learned the secret rites of creating a master rune… but whether you have the skill to successfully forge one still awaits to be seen. Choose a master rune from pages 127-131. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a master rune from the specified lists. 

You can use the _Forge Rune_ Endeavour to inscribe your chosen master rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new master rune you can craft. See page 121 for full runesmithing rules. In addition, the first time you acquire this Talent, you also learn all three Doom Runes (page 132). 

## **Maverick**
**Max** : Agility Bonus 

**Tests** : Sail (Skycraft) Tests to fly fast and dangerous You are an experienced, if reckless, flyer, putting your faith in high speed and overwhelming firepower. You do not suffer the -20 penalty on Ranged attacks when using the _Flight_ Creature Trait. 

## **Rune Magic**
**Max** : Intelligence Bonus + Willpower Bonus **Tests** : Runesmithing 

You are inducted into the secret arcane traditions of the Dwarfs, with the knowledge of crafting magical runes. 

Choose a rune from pages 127 - 131. You cannot select a master rune. If your Talent specifies a runic form or forms (e.g. Protection Runes), you must choose a rune from the specified lists. Finally, if your Talent specifies a specific rune (e.g. the Rune of Stone), you must choose that specific rune. 

You can use the _Forge Rune_ Endeavour to inscribe your chosen rune on an item. Each time you purchase this Talent, you learn a new rune you can craft. 

## **Short Fuse**
## **Max** : Intelligence Bonus
You time your explosives carefully to detonate at the optimum moment, showering fragments over the widest possible distance. When using an Explosive weapon with the _Blast_ Quality, increase its Rating by +1 for each level of Short Fuse. 

## **Tireless**
## **Max** : Toughness Bonus
You endure heavy burdens, tiring journeys, and interrupted sleep with admirable resolve, refusing to let such ordeals dull your mind or slow your fighting strength. 

When you apply penalties due to suffering from the Fatigued Condition, you may ignore 1 instance of the _Fatigued_ Condition, +1 additional _Fatigued_ Condition for each level of Tireless. For example, a Character with 4 _Fatigued_ Conditions and 2 levels of Tireless would ignore _Fatigued_ the effect of 3 Conditions, suffering only a -10 penalty to all Tests. 

## **Underminer**
**Max** : Agility Bonus 

**Tests** : You rarely have a height advantage over your enemies, but have learned to compensate by attacking from an unexpected angle. 

You do not suffer penalties for attacking whilst you have the _Prone_ Condition, or are otherwise beneath your target. Enemies do not get a bonus to attack you whilst you have the _Prone_ Condition. You gain an additional +20 to hit _Surprised_ enemies, when you are emerging from a tunnel, pit, or other hidden position below them. 

## **Whirlwind of Death**
## **Max** : 1
You attack in a sweeping, indiscriminate, fury, tearing through whole formations of enemy warriors. 

As an Action, you can spend 1 Fortune to make a Melee attack against all creatures Engaged with you. The GM chooses one enemy to Oppose this Test. If your attack succeeds, you inflict the same Damage to the same Hit Location against all Engaged creatures, calculated as normal. Do not apply Criticals on Whirlwind of Death attacks, though Critical Wounds are inflicted on enemies reduced to 0 Wounds as normal. 

You cannot activate any other special attack options as part of a Whirlwind of Death. However, if a Character with _Dual Wielder_ ( **WFRP Core Rulebook** ) is wielding two weapons as part of a Whirlwind of Death, they may Reverse their Melee attack Test. 

## **Grudges**
Amongst Dwarfs, Humans are renowned for their naive optimism. A Human, especially one confident enough to set off on adventures, views their life as a series of upcoming challenges to overcome, and makes plans based on an assumption of success. Whilst Humans look to the future, Dwarfs look to the past. They have little faith they will ever restore the fortunes of the Dwarfs’ golden age. Their priority is rarely to achieve something new, but to honour their ancestors by perpetuating the old ways… and to avenge any insults that have yet to be paid in kind. 

Grudges are an alternate system for Dwarf Characters to generate XP. They supersede the rules for Ambitions detailed in **WFRP Core Rulebook** . A Dwarf Character can track either Grudges or Ambitions, but not both — and a party of mostly Dwarf Characters must decide if they will be using Party Grudges or Party Ambitions. Though Dwarf Characters cannot gain XP through Ambitions, they still gain XP through end-of-session rewards, adventure rewards, or bonuses at the GM’s discretion. 

## **Recording Grudges**
A Grudge is a record of words or actions taken by another creature which have impugned a Dwarf ’s honour. Each Dwarf Character records their Grudges in a personal log, referred to as a Book of Grudges (or simply “book”). When recorded, a Grudge should specify the following: 

**A summary of the offence** which warranted the Grudge, e.g. spilling my pint; stealing my axe; killing my brother. A Grudge is not worth recording if appropriate restitution has already been obtained, e.g. you were bought a new drink; recovered your axe; or killed the creature responsible. 

**The perpetrator** , in as much as the Dwarf is able to identify them, e.g. Ralfa Facebruiser, the Silver Shakes gang, a goblin from the Red Eye tribe missing two front teeth. Grudges against groups, or very occasionally, inanimate objects, are also acceptable. 

**The restitution necessary to satisfy the Grudge** . Whilst the Grudges of kings and clan leaders carefully consider appropriate restitution with reference to legal precedent, individual Dwarfs (and players) are free to set whatever restitution they consider reasonable and proportionate to the severity of the grudge. 

If restitution is unreasonably low, the Dwarf may acquire a reputation as a pushover (and the player may deprive themselves of restitution benefits); if restitution is unreasonably high, the Dwarf will quickly acquire more Grudges than they are able to settle (and the player may deprive themselves of XP). 

**The date of the offence** . You should also leave space to record the date that the Grudge is satisfied. 

Once a Grudge is entered into your book, it cannot be removed except by satisfying the Grudge. Because Dwarf Characters can accumulate several Grudges over the course of their adventures, they may struggle to record all their Grudges on their character sheet. The Book of Grudges journal, sold separately, is perfect for the purpose of recording these Grudges. 

## **The Day of Grudgement**
Twice every century the Day of Grudgement is called. On this event the Dwarf kings from each hold travel to Karaza-Karak to report to the High King of new grudges to be written in the pages of the Dammaz Kron, or the happy news of the settling of an outstanding grudge which can be struck out. As the Dwarf empire is ever more beleaguered by its foes, the Day of Grudgement has become increasingly complicated, and the event can actually last for several weeks. 

## **Blood Grudge**
Some Grudges are much more serious than others. Grudges that demand the death of the perpetrator — those involving grievous harm, deliberate oath breaking, or monstrous creatures like Orcs, Goblins, Skaven, or followers of Chaos — are referred to as Blood Grudges. These Grudges are usually harder to settle, and impose more exacting effects on the Character when forced to interact with their perpetrators, but award more XP to Characters who successfully obtain satisfaction. 

## **Starting Grudges**
Instead of choosing a Short-term Ambition and Longterm Ambition in Stage 6 of Character Creation, a Dwarf Character can start with three Grudges. Record them in your book according to the process above. No more than one of these starting Grudges can be a Blood Grudge. 

As with Ambitions, it’s a good idea to talk to your GM when choosing your Grudges, so your GM can advise if you’ll get a reasonable chance to resolve the Grudge during the game. 

## **New Grudges**
At the end of each session, you can choose to gain a new Grudge. Choose an individual that insulted you during the session, and record the Grudge you bear against them per the usual process. 

Unlike Ambitions, you do not need to swap a Grudge for an existing Grudge that you have completed or abandoned. For this reason, it is possible for your book of Grudges to grow over the course of a campaign. 

If the entire session passes without an insult grievous enough to be entered in your book, you may still choose to enter a historic grievance as a Grudge. This refers to an incident that occurred off-screen, during downtime, or before play started, which has until this point not been relevant. As with starting Grudges, players should confer with the GM to ensure this new Grudge will have an opportunity to be pertinent during the game. 

If you should endure a session of such rage-inducing offences that you wish to enter multiple Grudges into your book, you can speak to your GM about adding more than one Grudge. For each additional Grudge you add into your book, you reduce the number of Fortune points you start the next session with by 1. You cannot add more additional Grudges than you have Fortune points to spend — if you find yourself in this situation, your GM may suggest consolidating your many grievances into a single Grudge that accommodates them all. 

## **Interacting with Perpetrators**
Dwarfs take their Grudges extremely personally. When interacting with an individual they bear a Grudge against, they find it difficult to think of anything but getting satisfaction. When interacting with an individual you bear a Grudge against, apply the _Animosity_ Psychology trait. When interacting with an individual you bear a Blood Grudge against, apply the _Hatred_ Psychology trait instead. See **WFRP Core Rulebook** for details. 

## **Resolving Grudges**
Grudges are resolved when you receive the restitution listed in your book. Update the Grudge by noting the date it was satisfied in your book. If you learn that the Grudge’s perpetrator has died without making recompense, the Grudge is inherited by their closest adult relative, liegelord, den mother, or undead master (as appropriate). A Blood Grudge is only satisfied if the perpetrator is slain by you, or allies and kin satisfying the Grudge on your behalf. 

A satisfied Grudge awards 25 XP. A satisfied Blood Grudges awards an additional +25 XP, for a total of 50 XP. 

## **Party Grudges**
If a group consists mostly of Dwarf Characters, they may choose to use Party Grudges rather than Party Ambitions. This reflects the group’s commitment to avenge wrongs paid to their party, their clan, their hold, or the Dwarf people as a whole. 

Instead of choosing a Short-term Party Ambition and Long-term Party Ambition in Stage 6 of Character Creation, a group of mostly Dwarf Characters can choose to start with three Party Grudges. Any number of these can be Blood Grudges. Dwarf Characters record Party Grudges in their books individually, in exactly the same way as personal Grudges, and agree between themselves what appropriate restitution should be. 

Party Grudges are resolved in the same way as personal Grudges. When all players agree the Grudge is settled, all Characters with the Grudge in their book earn 25 XP (an additional +25 XP for Blood Grudges), then marks the Grudge as satisfied. To acquire new Party Grudges, the whole group can choose to record the same Grudge as their personal Grudge for a session. 

Non-Dwarf Characters in a group with Party Grudges gain XP when the Party Grudges are satisfied, in the same way as their Dwarf companions. 

They also gain XP from the satisfaction of a Grudge that appears in the books of all Dwarf Characters in their party. However, non-Dwarf Characters do not track Grudges in their own book, do not apply the Psychological traits of interacting with Party Grudge perpetrators, and use personal Ambitions instead of personal Grudges. 

## **Unresolved Grudges**
Dwarfs do not subscribe to the vision of the afterlife evangelised by the priests of Morr. Instead, they believe that the spirits of their dead reside deep beneath the earth, in the Halls of the Ancestors, where they are judged by their gods and awarded a seat at the great feast table proportional to their deeds in life. It is said that Dwarfs with many Grudges left unresolved will be seated furthest from their most prestigious ancestors, and deprived of the best food and ale. 

If a Dwarf Character dies, their player’s new Character starts with additional XP, equal to half the XP the deceased Character acquired in play. However, this bonus XP is reduced by 25 XP for every outstanding Grudge the deceased Character had upon death, and reduced by an additional 25 XP (50 XP total) for every outstanding Blood Grudge. If the player’s new Character considers the deceased Character to be kin, any outstanding Grudges of the deceased Character are transferred directly into the new Character’s book of Grudges.
